findings.failure_scenario: Input print("{}\x61".format(data)): the literal \x61 decodes to 'a', so the map rewrites every 'a' in the converted f"{data}a" to f"{d\x61t\x61}\x61" — invalid Python, so api.py's final ast.parse fails and the ENTIRE file's conversion is skipped (this file converted fine before the change). Worse, print("{}\n\x6e".format(x)) yields f"{x}\\x6e\x6e", which parses fine (ast.parse passes, statement count unchanged) but evaluates to backslash+'x6e'+'n' instead of newline+'n' — a silent behavior change written to disk. Similar: "a{}\x7b".format(x) turns the f-string's own braces into \x7b escapes, changing the produced string; "{}\x66".format(x) replaces the 'f' prefix itself.
findings.summary: apply_unicode_escape_map substitutes mapped characters across the ENTIRE converted f-string source — delimiters, {expression} braces, identifiers, and the \n/\t/\\ escape text that fixup_transformed generates — so any \xNN/\u/\U/\N{} escape that decodes to an ASCII syntax character (letters, digits, quotes, braces, backslash, n, t) corrupts the output.

findings.failure_scenario: Input print("{}".format(s.replace("x", "\x61"))): the \x61 inside the format argument produces map entry a → \x61; the converted f-string f"{s.replace('x', 'a')}" is rewritten to f"{s.repl\x61ce('x', '\x61')}" — a SyntaxError, so the whole file's conversion is silently dropped (status 'failed', file unmodified). Phantom entries: "a\\u00B0{}".format(x) matches \u00B0 at the second backslash of the escaped-backslash pair even though the string's value contains no degree sign, and "%s" % (A + "\x41") maps 'A' from the operand.
findings.summary: unicode_escape_map builds the mapping from the whole chunk text (body = literal[idx+len(quote):-len(quote)]), which retains the closing quote and the entire .format(...) argument list / % operand, so escapes inside arguments — or a \\u00B0-style escaped backslash — become mapping entries that get substituted into the converted expression code.

findings.failure_scenario: Non-behavioral: the function duplicates unicode_escape_re.search logic with no caller, so it adds an unused public API that must be maintained and can drift out of sync with unicode_escape_map's actual escape handling (e.g. if the regex is extended, this function's semantics change with no consumer to exercise them).
findings.summary: contains_unicode_escape is dead code: exported by this change but never referenced anywhere in src/ or test/ (grep confirms zero callers).

findings.failure_scenario: Non-behavioral: every breakage mode above (\xNN ASCII escapes, quote/brace/backslash escapes, escapes in .format arguments, phantom mappings from \\ escapes) passes CI unnoticed because no test asserts the output for them; the new unit test drives CodeEditor.edit() directly, which bypasses api.py's whole-file ast.parse validation, so corrupted output like f"{d\x61t\x61}\x61" would be returned and could be asserted without any error being raised.
findings.summary: The added tests cover only the collision-free \u00B0 case (unit test) and, in the integration pair, an escaped-backslash case whose string VALUE contains no escape at all (samples_in/unicode_escape.py contains '\\u00B0' — two backslashes — so the feature never engages); none of the mechanism's failure modes are exercised.
